transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 13:45 UTC
Duration: 43m
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Maven Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (Maven Platform Eng), Daniel Park (Maven CTO)

00:00 Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan, AE on the account and with me is Priya from our performance team. How's everyone doing?
00:05 Liam: Good, thanks. Excited to dig in — we've been evaluating options for replacing a homegrown inference layer. Main focus today is latency and throughput, p95 targets, and what Dedicated vs Hosted would look like.
00:13 Priya: Great. Quick agenda — we want to understand your p95 targets, concurrency needs, streaming requirements, and then we'll map those to Redwood hosting modes and a benchmark plan.
00:20 Sofia: Perfect. I pulled some numbers — current production is about 120 qps steady with 300 qps bursts, typical request is single-turn chat-like prompt to a 7B open model, average response length 120 tokens, and our observed p95 end-to-end is ~700ms but we want <250ms p95 ideally for UI snappiness.
00:40 Priya: Ok that's helpful. A couple clarifying q's — when you say 120 qps steady, what's the concurrency? Do you mean 120 active requests concurrently or 120 requests per second with short tails?
00:48 Sofia: It's about 80 concurrent on average. Spiky traffic when marketing runs promos goes up to ~260 concurrent for a few minutes.
00:54 Ethan: Good, so rough requirement: p95 <250ms at up to 200-260 concurrency, streaming for partial token display, and cost needs to be predictable. Correct?
01:02 Daniel: Yes. Also security constraints — we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, and VPC peering for Private deployment options. Data residency for EU customers is important.
01:10 Priya: Sounds standard. For p95 <250ms at that concurrency, we usually recommend Dedicated capacity or Private with pinned GPUs, because Hosted is great for most use cases but can exhibit more variance during noisy neighbor events unless you reserve Dedicated. We can also do autoscaling with predictable tail latencies but there are trade-offs.
01:28 Liam: Can you give an example with numbers? Like tokens/sec per GPU and what concurrency a single node can handle?
01:32 Priya: Sure. Ballpark numbers depend heavily on model, quantization, sequence length, and runtime kernel. For a 7B model with q4_0 quantization on A100-style hardware, we've seen steady-state generation rates of 150-300 tokens/sec per GPU for generation-only (no heavy custom ops), with lower latency per token when using streaming.
01:50 Priya: If your average response is 120 tokens, at 150 tokens/sec that's ~0.8s of pure generation time per request. But with Redwood's continuous batching and KV cache for multi-turns, effective latency can be lower for short responses. Also p95 includes request queuing and routing so you need reserved concurrency or sufficient instances to avoid queuing.
02:10 Sofia: That generation time seems high — we need <250ms p95. Is that achievable?
02:14 Priya: For single-turn short outputs (like 30 tokens), yes — at 300 tokens/sec that's 0.1s generation. But for 120 token responses you'll need model size and quantization trade-offs or use a smaller distilled model, or shard across more GPUs. Another lever is streaming: if you stream partial tokens to the client, perceived latency (time-to-first-token) can be under 150ms even if total generation takes longer.
02:34 Liam: So we should aim to optimize time-to-first-token rather than full completion for UX. Can Redwood guarantee p95 time-to-first-token?
02:40 Priya: We can set up SLOs and prioritized routing to minimize time-to-first-token — Dedicated capacity with warm KV caches and hot instances pinned to your tenant is our recommended path for strict p95s. In Hosted you can also buy higher SLA tiers but for very tight p95 at high concurrency Dedicated gives the most control.
02:56 Ethan: Quick note on batching — we do continuous batching inside the runtime. That increases throughput and lowers per-token cost, but batching adds a small scheduling delay which can impact p50 more than p95 if we size the batch window aggressively. We can tune batching to favor latency (smaller windows) at the cost of some throughput.
03:14 Daniel: What about token/sec benchmark methodology — we want to reproduce results locally. What's the plan?
03:18 Priya: We recommend a 3-step benchmark: 1) run single-instance microbench (cold start and warm), 2) run concurrency ramp to simulate your 120 steady + 260 burst profile, and 3) run streaming time-to-first-token tests with your real prompts. We'll use your sample prompts and sequence lengths to get realistic tokens/sec. We'll run on model variants you care about (7B, 13B) and on quantized variants.
03:40 Sofia: Can Redwood run that for us or do we run it in our infra?
03:44 Priya: We can run an initial benchmark in our Dedicated staging environment. For Private/on-prem we'd provide a benchmark harness you can run. For Hosted, we can simulate traffic against hosted endpoints but results may differ slightly due to multi-tenant noise.
03:59 Ethan: Action item: Priya will run the initial token/sec benchmark using Maven sample prompts and return results with p50/p95/p99 breakdowns.
04:07 Liam: On security — how do you handle KMS, encryption, logs? We need KMS integration and ability to rotate keys, plus audit logs for every request.
04:14 Ethan: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations, and we can enable customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available in Redwood Console with retention options. We'll share our SOC 2 docs and network arch.
04:25 Daniel: Good. Also data residency — we need EU-only processing for certain customers. Is that possible?
04:29 Priya: Yes — routing policies can pin requests to region or Dedicated pools; Private gives the strongest guarantee for physical location. We also support per-route routing rules so EU traffic stays in EU.
04:38 Sofia: Regarding cost — can you share rough cost math? e.g., if we need 6 A100-like GPUs dedicated, what's expected monthly ballpark vs hosted?
04:47 Ethan: We'll model two paths: Hosted pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing (we'll show examples for your traffic), and Dedicated which is reserved monthly capacity — usually cheaper per-token for sustained usage but with commit. We'll include burst strategies and autoscaling costs in the sheet.
05:00 Liam: One more thing — fallback behavior. If Dedicated is saturated, can redirects happen to a Hosted pool of lower tier?
05:06 Priya: Yes, we have smart routing and fallbacks — you can set policy to fallback to compatible model variants or hosted pools. We also support canary rollouts and A/B test deployments.
05:14 Ethan: Ok let's dig into a couple of hypothetical numbers to size infra. If your p95 target is 250ms and average token length is 120, the straightforward way is to reduce model cost per response by using smaller model or reduce tokens, or aim for perceived latency via streaming. If you insist on full-response p95 <250ms for 120 tokens, you'd need extremely high tokens/sec — roughly 480 tokens/sec to finish in 0.25s — that typically implies many GPUs or a smaller model. So we need to align on realistic SLOs.
05:46 Daniel: That's helpful — maybe we re-evaluate UX expectations. Time-to-first-token <150ms and full completion within 800ms could be acceptable for some flows. We'll put down which flows need strict snappiness.
05:56 Sofia: We will share the traffic breakdown per endpoint and which flows are latency-sensitive.
06:00 Priya: Great. For benchmarking we'll target both time-to-first-token and full-response p95. We'll include streaming metrics (tTF token, tTFP for first 4 tokens, etc.), tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens for each deployment mode.
06:15 Liam: How much does quantization affect tokens/sec? 8-bit vs 4-bit?
06:19 Priya: Q4 variants often yield 1.5x-2x improvement in throughput on the same hardware compared to full-fp16, but may slightly change output fidelity. We recommend running evals on your prompt set to measure quality regressions. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload.
06:36 Ethan: Anything else on requirements?
06:38 Liam: SLA — we need 99.95% for dedicated workloads ideally. Also single-tenant isolation for PCI scope might be required.
06:45 Priya: Dedicated can be SLA-backed and single-tenant. For strict PCI scope you may prefer Private on VPC or on-prem. We'll put details in the security docs.
06:55 Sofia: Alright — summary and next steps from our side?
07:00 Ethan: Recap: 1) Priya runs benchmarks against sample prompts (time-to-first-token and full p95) in Dedicated staging. 2) Ethan sends pricing + example cost models for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. 3) Maven to share traffic profiles and which endpoints require snappy UX. 4) Redwood to send SOC2, KMS & network docs.
07:19 Daniel: Sounds good. Can we schedule the 1-hour workshop for the week of 3/9?
07:22 Priya: Yes I'll send a Doodle after the call.
07:25 Liam: Thanks folks.
07:26 Ethan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the attachments and the benchmark plan.
07:30 (call ends)

Notes: transcription has occasional phrase errors; speaker turns approximate. References: shared drive link to benchmark spreadsheet (drive.redwood/example-benchmarks), SOC2 doc link (redwood.example/soc2.pdf), sample pricing sheet (redwood.example/pricing/maven-models.xlsx).
